To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

antibodies against six individual herpes virus antigens can be detected by quantitative immunoelectropheresis, that the antibody titers correlate with neutralization titers, that the antibodies against Ag8 and Ag 11 account for the majority of the cross-reactivity between herpes simplex virus type 1 and 2, and that antibodies against Ag4, Ag6, Ag9 and Ag11 are type-specific.
antibodies against the two HSV type-common glycopeptides D and B are responsible for the serological crossreactivity between HSV type I and type II.
the glycoprotein Ag8 and Ag 11, both containing glycosylate polypeptides D (Ag8) and B (Ag11), were found to be the major targets of human antibodies against HSV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a quantitative immunochemical method for the analysis of human antibodies to HSV.
the development of a quantitative immunoelectrophoretical method for analysis of human antibody response to HSV antigens, and we have shown that the method is suitable for this purpose.
the development of quantitative immunological techniques for the analysis of the humoral immune response to HSV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HSV neutralizing antibodies are directed against a large number of different glycoproteins, some of which are shared by both HSV type 1- and type 2, and that the neutralization of HSV by antibodies is a multivalent process.
the glycoproteins Ag8 and Ag6 of HSV 1 and the glycoproteines Ag11, 9, and 4 of HSV 2 contain the most immunogenic determinants.
the most immunogenic HSV glycoproteins are Ag8 and Ag6 (glycoprotein D and C, respectively) and that the anti-Ag8 antibody titers correlate best with the HSV neutralizing antibody titer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
quantitative analysis of antibodies against individual herpes simplex virus proteins is a useful tool in the study of the human immune response to this virus.
the use of quantitative crossed immunoelectroprophoresis with intermediate gels is an efficient method to study antibodies to herpes simplex virus glycoproteins in human sera.
the glycoprotein antigens of HSV can be used as markers of the humoral immune response in human HSV infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of crossed immunoprecipitation with intermediate gel is a useful tool for the quantitative analysis of human antibodies to HSV.
the use of a quantitative method for the determination of antibody titers is a prerequisite for the development of diagnostic reagent systems.
the use of a quantitative immunoelectrophoretical method for determination of antibody titers against individual HSV glycoproteins can be recommended for diagnostic purposes.
